I'd land on N for both Agency and Clarity, but flag this as a genuine boundary case. The not-knowing is honest and openly stated, which works against both Clarity miscalibration and Agency foreclosure. Casey isn't pretending to know, isn't treating anything as settled, and isn't withdrawing from participation — they're accurately reporting that they've reached the limit of what they can currently articulate or ask for. That's a speaker being precise about the edges of their own capacity, which is uncomfortable but not deficient under any of the four components.

The taxonomy's resolution indicators in §4.4 are useful here. One marker of Clarity repair is "the speaker acknowledges a self-contradiction and reconciles it." Logan isn't fully reconciling — the turn cuts off before resolution — but they're doing the first half of that work: identifying and naming the contradiction. A speaker who flags their own incongruence in real time is performing self-directed Clarity maintenance, not exhibiting a Clarity deficit.

The Acknowledgement label is right — "I'm not saying that to make you feel bad" is preemptive hedging, and "I stopped because I figured" retroactively frames the earlier self-suppression as something Casey already knew was necessary, carrying a self-as-wronged quality. But the flattened affect, clipped delivery, and the fact that Casey is explaining why they already stopped rather than re-raising the concern suggests this turn may be sitting on the Acknowledgement-to-Agency transition described in §1.5 — the bids have ceased but what's replaced them is flat resignation rather than engagement. I'd keep Acknowledgement as primary but flag Agency as a secondary candidate worth tracking in subsequent turns.

Acknowledgement: Y. Jordan's turn exhibits the core §1.1 pattern: self-minimizing language paired with continued investment ("I'm not trying to make this into something bigger than it needs to be" followed by sustained disclosure), an explicit bid for recognition ("I need you to understand where I'm at"), and self-as-subject framing throughout — the turn is organized around Jordan's experience of the situation, not around a demand or an attack. Not Reciprocity: Jordan's fairness claim is legitimate assertiveness under §3.5, leaving the form of resolution open and closing with an invitation to joint sense-making rather than staking a fixed position. Not Agency: Jordan's turn shows sustained investment and initiative rather than constraint language, deferral, or withdrawal. Not Clarity: Jordan's account is concrete and observation-proximate (specific day, specific sensory detail, specific sequence of events), with no epistemic miscalibration or unverified attribution.

N across all four components. The self-minimizing language ("I'm not trying to make this harder than it needs to be") and hedging ("I genuinely don't know how you're going to read it") have the surface form of Acknowledgement and Agency signals, but in context they read as situationally normal politeness in an asymmetric institutional interaction rather than as evidence of unmet recognition needs or foreclosed participation. Kendall's turns across the window have been consistently substantive and engaged — no escalating recognition bids, no progressive shortening or deferral, no constraint narratives — and the hedging around categorization is the same accurate epistemic signaling Kendall has been performing throughout, not a retreat from participation.

Taylor's turn exhibits a consistent pattern of positional holding wrapped in a measured, professional register. The core structure is a repeated open-and-close: Taylor identifies something in the documentation that could matter ("the functional piece specifically"), then immediately brackets it within fixed constraints — the existing offer doesn't move, the supplemental process runs separately, it takes time, it may not produce a different outcome. Each partial concession is followed by a re-closure that forecloses collaborative exploration. Throughout the turn, Taylor presents outcomes as settled rather than as interests open to discussion, never asks what the other party needs or what the functional limitation means from their perspective, and parcels out procedural knowledge in a way that manages expectations downward rather than creating transparency.

There's also an Acknowledgement boundary question the rationale doesn't address. The self-minimizing language is notable — "which is probably not a great sign," "I don't want this to be a whole thing," "I'll own that." Logan is hedging around the disclosure, softening preemptively, signaling anxiety about how this will land. Under §1.1, self-minimizing language where the speaker downplays the legitimacy of their concern while still pursuing it is an Acknowledgement signal. The case for labeling it here is weak, though, because this is turn 0 — there's no window showing these hedges to be part of an escalating pattern of unmet recognition bids, and the §1.3 default applies. The hedging could equally be politeness, conflict-aversion, or early-stage framing. N is the right call, but it's worth flagging as something to watch in subsequent turns.

The model reads Jules's constraint language — "not something I have the same room on," "that's the position I'm in" — as Agency, but the turn isn't exhibiting perceived powerlessness. Jules is delivering a structured, confident denial with a clear rationale, validating Quinn's experience while explaining a consistency principle they've internalized and are actively administering. Agency speakers retreat; Jules is advancing an institutional argument. The constraint language functions as professional positioning — explaining why the policy applies — not as felt foreclosure of the speaker's capacity to shape the outcome. All four components are N.

The model reads Quinn's "probably the original booking, that's usually how it is" as resigned foreclosure — preemptively surrendering the one remaining avenue. But Quinn is answering a factual question with honest uncertainty, not abandoning a bid. "I'd have to check, I'm not sure offhand" is accurate epistemic signaling, and "probably the original booking" is a provisional estimate based on travel experience, not a motivational collapse. The difference between "it probably won't help so why bother" (Agency) and "I'd have to check but I think the answer is X" (just answering the question) is the difference between foreclosure and good-faith recollection. All four N.

The model reads "yeah, I'll check" as nominal participation consistent with progressive deferral. But brevity alone isn't a deficit — it needs constraint language, powerless markers, or withdrawal from the speaker's own baseline. Jules just offered a concrete next step (send the original itinerary and I'll look again), and "I'll check" is the proportionate, conversationally appropriate response to that offer. More importantly, it's structurally opposite to foreclosure — Quinn is accepting a reopened pathway and committing to a follow-through action, not withdrawing. Short turns that represent forward motion aren't the same as short turns that represent disengagement. All four N.

The model finds Clarity deficit in Logan saying $200 "shouldn't tank what you're trying to save," calling it overcertainty about Jules's financial situation. But that's a rough contextualizing assessment meant to soften the number, not an unverified assumption being treated as established fact — the phrasing is hedged and the intent is transparently to invite further discussion. The turn is doing significant repair work: naming a concrete number (which Jules specifically requested), owning the prior miscommunication, validating Jules's understanding, articulating the underlying interest about separating work and living, and explicitly framing the figure as something to talk about rather than a fixed position. All four N.
